text:
maria: :rotating_light: incidents-bot alerted - multiple CUDA OOMs on serving-prod-gpu-11 despite ~2GB headroom reserved. Errors started ~10:12 UTC. Seeing container restarts + node flaps.

incidents-bot: [ALERT] gpu-mem-pressure HIGH on node serving-prod-gpu-11. Recent events: container_restart x3, nvml OOM reports.

sam: Oncall here, stepping in. @maria can you paste the first failure log and nvml output? Also need high-level customer impact now.

maria: paste below - truncated logs from runtime on node:

```
2026-03-14T10:12:09Z runtime: allocate(524288000) failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
stack: runtime/alloc.cpp:231
model_server: attempting reserve_pool(2gb)
allocator: reserved_blocks=6 used=4 free=2
nvml: process 3245 (model_worker) gpu_mem=6.8GB, driver_reported_free=2.1GB
```

jorge: quick check of node before we restart: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.free --format=csv` returned:

```
memory.used [MiB], memory.free [MiB]
8420 MiB, 2100 MiB
```

jorge: but driver free doesn't match allocator free. Looks like allocator fragmentation / stuck reserved blocks. Could be KV cache pinning or stale CUDA allocations in crashed containers.

liz: We're seeing spike in 429/500 rate on the region. P50 latency + tail increased. Customer impact: ~12 tenants seeing degraded throughput; error rate ~9% over baseline. Adding to incident timeline.

sam: mitigation plan: 1) reduce concurrency on node (scale down pool); 2) disable KV prefix cache on the node to free pinned blocks; 3) if still OOM, drain + restart node. Any objections?

maria: no objections. I have a live command to disable in-proc cache: set env `RW_KV_CACHE_ENABLED=false` and roll the worker. Will do a targeted roll on serving-prod-gpu-11 only.

jorge: before killing, check for orphaned CUDA allocations: `ps aux | grep model_worker` then `sudo lsof -p <pid> | grep /dev/nvidia` and `docker inspect` to see if containers left stale handles. I found one crashed container still present with PID 4321 holding 1.2GB.

maria: stopped that process (PID 4321) and forced docker rm. Re-checking nvml: `memory.free` went up ~600MiB, but we're still hitting OOMs under load.

kevin: I'm moving 30% of traffic off node to serving-prod-gpu-4 (same region) via routing override. Doing canary shift now.

deploy-bot: Rollout started: set RW_KV_CACHE_ENABLED=false on pool serving-prod-gpu-11 (20 instances) by maria.

maria: rollout finished on 11/20 workers. Observed immediate reclaim of ~1GB across those processes. Errors dropped but not eliminated.

sam: still seeing occasional OOMs at higher sequence lengths (~8k tokens). Hypothesis: allocator has reserved blocks sized for common seq len; fragmentation increases when we hit long sequences and can't coalesce. Also observed reserves not freed because reserve_eviction wasn't triggered.

jorge: quick mitigation: enable aggressive reserve eviction for this node only: `RW_RESERVE_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.3` and `RW_RESERVE_EVICT_STEP=2`. This forces larger evictions when free falls below 30%. Patching now.

maria: applied env vars and restarted affected workers (rolling).

liz: monitoring: errors fell to ~1.2% and latency stabilized. Customer-impacting errors went down significantly. Still 1 tenant seeing occasional errors when sequences >9k.

sam: decision: keep node in service but reduce max-concurrency and keep reserve-evict aggressive. If we see repeat OOMs in 30m, drain + reprovision. Assigning follow-up owner for postmortem.

kevin: I'm preparing a warm replacement node in the pool with updated allocator config (larger min_block_size and more aggressive coalescing). Will swap out if needed.

maria: quick note - root cause likely a combination: 1) fragmentation from mixed sequence-length traffic, 2) stale pinned allocations from crashed containers + KV cache pinning, and 3) reserve eviction defaults too conservative for this workload.

sam: customer impact summary for pager duty: ~12 tenants degraded, peak error rate +9%, overall P0 mitigated. No data exfiltration. Tentative severity: Sev2 (partial degradation).

liz: I'll notify CS + sales with the impact summary and list of affected tenants.

jorge: logs to capture for postmortem: allocator stats, nvml queries every 10s, docker ps tree during incident, and a sample of long sequence traces that triggered OOM path.

maria: created follow-up ticket INF-1428 for postmortem and long-term fixes: increase reserve-evict aggressiveness by default, add auto-detection for long-sequence bursts to temporarily bump min_block_size, and more aggressive stale-handle cleanup on container crash.

sam: handoff: I'm oncall for next 30m. If no regression, we'll close this incident and schedule PM/Eng sync. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks everyone. I'll draft the incident summary and add timelines + mitigation steps to INF-1428.

incidents-bot: Incident acknowledged. Templates: please fill in impact, timeline, root-cause, mitigation, and action items.

kevin: quick note for the postmortem - attach `nvidia-smi` histograms and the allocator debug dumps we collected to the ticket.

sam: closing note: main takeaways - reserve blocks can be misleading when driver reports headroom; fragmentation + pinned allocations can cause effective OOM. We need better instrumentation to show allocator vs driver free clearly in the console.
